wage_series_reference: average_monthly_salaries.csv; pre-1992 observations use historical_manufacturing_hourly_wages.csv where available

sources.source: Statistics Sweden (SCB), average monthly salary after sector, all sectors, total gender.
sources.unit: SEK/month; annual comparator calculated as monthly × 12
sources.definition: SCB average monthly salary across all sectors, both sexes (total gender), for each year 1992–2025. Salary is not disposable income or actual annual earnings.
sources.transformation: Annual comparator is monthly average multiplied by 12; nominal values. Monthly source values retained in the separate salary file.

sources.source: Sveriges Riksbank, Historical Monetary and Financial Statistics for Sweden, Volume I, Svante Prado workbook, Tables I.A10.1 and I.A10.2.
sources.definition: Hourly earnings by manufacturing industry category and sex, plus a separately identified source-provided weighted average. Source table categories are represented in Swedish in the CSV.
sources.coverage: Sweden; manufacturing workers. Coverage varies by industry and sex. Male categories are observed from 1860 or later depending on category; female coverage starts between 1865 and 1952 by category. Male weighted average 1871–2013; female weighted average 1921–2013.
sources.transformation: Transcribed source observations without annualization or interpolation. Missing cells are omitted. This sectoral hourly series is not directly equivalent to all-sector monthly salary; overlap does not imply equivalent population or method.

sources.source: Swedish Nintendo price observations from dated retail catalogues/advertisements (1987, 1991–1994), plus annual Swedish sales volumes and sales values by Nintendo platform from Dataspelsbranschen reports (1998–2015).
sources.unit: Nominal SEK/game where documented; 2010–2015 nominal EUR/game only
sources.definition: Nominal SEK per game. Two observation types are kept distinct: sparse arithmetic means of listed new-game prices in dated retailer advertisements/catalogues (not market means), and weighted average consumer expenditure per sold Nintendo software unit calculated by summing reported sales value and units across Nintendo platforms in Sweden. The annual reports cover physical game sales, exclude hardware and do not include digital sales.
sources.coverage: Catalogue observations: 1987, 1991, 1992 (three samples), 1993 and 1994. Weighted Nintendo sales averages: each year 1998–2015. No verified catalogue price for 1988–1990 or 1995–1997; no comparable annual Nintendo unit/value dataset found for 2016–2026. Official-distributor brochure scans reviewed for 1988–1993 are game lists, not price lists. The 1990 Datormagazin examples at 398 SEK are in a hypothetical reader letter and are excluded. Current Tradera asking/listing prices indexed by original release year (for example Retrospel.nu) are second-hand market prices today, not original launch-year prices, and are excluded.
sources.transformation: Catalogue sample means divide the sum of listed nominal retail prices by the count of priced titles; seller/platform/sample details are in each row. For 1998–2009, annual reported value (SEK) and units for all Nintendo platforms in Sweden were summed and divided; the 2009 report says distributor-to-retailer data were converted to estimated consumer expenditure including VAT and warns that they are not directly comparable with later GfK retail sell-through. For 2010–2015, reported Nintendo platform EUR values are summed and divided by reported units, retained only as EUR/game. Audit 2026-11-16 withdrew the previous conversion using annual-average EUR/SEK: 2010–2014 reports print point-date conversion rates, and 2015 does not establish the necessary SEK conversion basis. No SEK price, wage share or trend is published for these six observations. No inflation adjustment. Reported units are sample_size for these rows; catalogue rows use number of priced titles. Price shares use SCB all-sector mean monthly salary × 12 for 1992 onward; pre-1992 samples use the separately identified Riksbank male manufacturing hourly wage × 2,080 where available, which is not directly comparable. No interpolation; unobserved years remain gaps.
sources.verification_limitations: Audit 2026-11-16: seven catalogue means cannot be fully independently recalculated because individual title-price transcriptions are absent; the 1992 issue 13 PDF URL returned 404. Retained values remain qualified source samples, not newly fully verified statistics. Historical report labels include Game Boy Advance in 2000, preceding hardware release; aggregate values follow the source as reported and do not establish platform release dates.

sources.source: Nördliv, dated price statements in reviews explicitly identifying the tested Nintendo Switch / Switch 2 version; original quoted sources are Prisjakt, Nintendo/eShop and DekuDeals. These are secondary reported price observations, not transaction-level official statistics.
sources.unit: nominal SEK/game; reported lowest price per title at the source-stated date
sources.definition: Unweighted arithmetic mean per observation year of retained exact SEK lowest-price quotations for Nintendo Switch/Switch 2 games in Swedish reviews. Both Nintendo and third-party games, physical retail and digital eShop quotations. The sources do not separately document VAT per quote; no tax adjustment or foreign currency conversion is applied. Excludes hardware, accessories, subscriptions and add-ons.
sources.coverage: Swedish review sample, each year 2017–2026 through retrieval date 2026-11-16; 61 retained title-price observations, 2–10 per year. No eligible observation found for 2016. This is neither a complete annual catalogue nor a sales-weighted or representative national annual price average. 2026 is incomplete and has no annual salary comparison.
sources.transformation: Sum exact observed SEK amounts within year / count of titles, rounded to öre; computed by the pipeline from the individual observation CSV. Retain source URL, source-stated observation date, publication date, platform and exact price statement for every title. Inclusion: explicit tested Switch version; exact SEK amount; named price source; source-stated price date in publication year and no later than publication, at most 45 days before publication. Exclude approximate amounts, foreign currency, contradictory years/dates and prices explicitly for another platform. Yearly selection and channel mix vary, so no year-to-year trend is calculated. 2026 salary is missing, preserved as null; no extrapolation.

data.price_basis: Arithmetic mean: 12 titles shown in a Milu Handels AB flyer dated 1987 by the archive seller; each cassette listed at 289 SEK. Dated single-retailer flyer, not a national or annual market mean
data.wage_basis: Riksbank historical male weighted-average manufacturing hourly wage × 2,080 hours (40 × 52); not comparable to SCB all-sector salary

data.price_basis: Arithmetic mean: 51 NES game prices in Larkman Computer Center catalogue/advertisement in Datormagazin issue 6/91; nominal listed SEK, issue dated 1991, not a market-wide annual mean
data.wage_basis: Riksbank historical male weighted-average manufacturing hourly wage × 2,080 hours (40 × 52); not comparable to SCB all-sector salary

data.price_basis: Arithmetic mean of 26 original-packaged NES titles in Aintronic's Datormagazin 13/92 catalogue advertisement; prices incl. 25% VAT, postage and handling extra; 1992 issue-specific retailer sample
data.wage_basis: SCB average monthly salary, all sectors, total gender × 12

data.price_basis: Arithmetic mean of 10 individually listed SNES games in Aintronic's Datormagazin 13/92 catalogue advertisement; excludes Super Scope 6-game pack; prices incl. 25% VAT, postage and handling extra; 1992 issue-specific retailer sample
data.wage_basis: SCB average monthly salary, all sectors, total gender × 12

data.price_basis: Arithmetic mean: 44 priced SNES titles in Landsbergs Spel & Data advertisement in Datormagazin issue 17/92; all listed at 499 SEK incl. VAT, some marked 'out soon'; mail-order postage/fees extra, not a market-wide annual mean
data.wage_basis: SCB average monthly salary, all sectors, total gender × 12

data.price_basis: Unweighted mean of 17 advertised SNES titles in a Swedish mail-order catalogue; listed selling prices, not a market-wide mean
data.wage_basis: SCB average monthly salary, all sectors, total gender × 12

data.price_basis: Unweighted mean of 9 SNES games explicitly listed as new in a Swedish mail-order advertisement; seller describes its prices as low mail-order prices, not a market-wide mean
